title: Severe droughts affect critical shipping arteries, sending more disruption to energy markets
gist: El Niño-driven drought is simultaneously constraining the Panama Canal (transits down to ~271/day in late May, partial recovery to ~308 in June) and the Rhine (Kaub at a record-low 15 cm on 11 August, barges at ~25% capacity), stacking a second and third freight shock on top of a Strait of Hormuz closure that has already removed ~20% of global LNG supply. Wood Mackenzie's VesselTracker data frames LNG as the most exposed commodity because its arbitrage margins are narrowest, with Rotterdam-Frankfurt barge rates up more than fivefold to EUR 150 per tonne.

insights.claim: The closure of the Strait of Hormuz has removed approximately 20% of global LNG supply, and Panama Canal drought restrictions now add a second, independent constraint that squeezes Pacific LNG buyers from two directions at once.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Two uncorrelated supply/logistics shocks compounding in the same commodity argue for owning JKM upside or LNG shipping exposure rather than assuming mean reversion in either shock alone.
insights.quote: Asian LNG markets are navigating the downstream effects of the Strait of Hormuz closure, which has removed approximately 20% of global LNG supply

insights.claim: Drought conditions can inflate freight costs and tighten vessel availability even when underlying supply and demand fundamentals are completely unchanged, meaning logistics is an independent price driver in energy commodities.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Model freight and chokepoint capacity as a separate risk factor from S/D balances; fundamentals-only models will systematically underprice these episodes.
insights.quote: The result is higher tonne-mile demand, tighter vessel availability, and elevated freight costs, even when underlying supply and demand fundamentals are unchanged.
insights.locator: LNG, LPG, and refined products bear

insights.claim: Among energy commodities, LNG is the most sensitive to canal constraints because its arbitrage margins are narrow, followed by LPG and refined product flows where even modest freight increases can close trading windows.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: A sensitivity ranking for positioning: freight shocks hit LNG arbitrage first, so watch US Gulf-to-Asia spreads as the leading indicator of cargo rerouting.
insights.quote: Among energy commodities, LNG is the most sensitive given narrow arbitrage margins, followed by LPG and product flows where even modest freight increases can close trading windows.
insights.locator: Among energy commodities, LNG is the most sensitive

insights.claim: Daily Panama Canal transits fell from approximately 325 per day in early May to as low as 271 in late May, then only partially recovered to about 308 per day through June.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: A hard, trackable throughput series; a failure to regain the ~325/day baseline is the quantitative trigger for sustained tonne-mile inflation.
insights.quote: Daily transits at the Panama Canal fell from approximately 325 per day in early May to as low as 271 in late May before partially recovering to approximately 308 per day through June

insights.claim: The incomplete recovery in Panama Canal transits signals a tightening corridor rather than a normalising one, implying the constraint should be treated as structural for the coming quarters rather than a passing weather event.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Argues against fading the freight spike; position for persistence into Q3/Q4 rather than a snapback.
insights.quote: The pattern signals a tightening corridor rather than a normalising one.

insights.claim: Rainfall deficits have forced Panama Canal authorities to impose draft restrictions that reduce effective vessel carrying capacity, so headline transit counts understate the true loss of cargo throughput.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Transit counts alone are a misleading gauge; the capacity hit is transits multiplied by reduced per-vessel load.
insights.locator: El Niño-driven drought conditions are restricting

insights.claim: Panama Canal water levels have fallen to their lowest reading compared with both 2025 and the five-year average, marking a deterioration versus recent history rather than a normal seasonal dip.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Benchmarking against the five-year average removes seasonality as an excuse and supports treating this as a genuine tail event.
insights.locator: El Niño-driven drought conditions are restricting

insights.claim: When Panama Canal draft restrictions bind, carriers have only three options - load below capacity, compete for transit slots, or reroute via the Cape of Good Hope, which adds roughly 10 to 15 days to voyage times.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Each branch is bullish tonne-mile demand and charter rates; a 10-15 day detour effectively removes vessels from the available fleet.
insights.quote: carriers either load below capacity, compete for transit slots, or reroute via the Cape of Good Hope, adding approximately 10 to 15 days to voyage times
insights.locator: LNG, LPG, and refined products bear

insights.claim: The Panama Canal is the specific link between US Gulf Coast export terminals and Pacific basin demand centres, so canal stress directly reprices the US-to-Asia leg rather than global freight uniformly.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Focus exposure on US Gulf export economics and Asian import parity, not on generic global shipping indices.
insights.locator: LNG, LPG, and refined products bear

insights.claim: The water level at Kaub, the Rhine's critical chokepoint for barge navigation in western Germany, dropped to just 15 cm on 11 August from 30 cm on 28 July - the lowest level on record.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: A record low at the single gauge that governs European inland energy logistics; Kaub is the number to watch for German refining and product distribution stress.
insights.quote: The water level at Kaub, the Rhine's critical chokepoint for barge navigation in western Germany, dropped to just 15 cm on 11 August, down from 30 cm on 28 July, the lowest level on record.

insights.claim: Most Rhine barges were operating at around 25% of their cargo capacity as of 12 August, an effective 75% loss of inland European energy transport capacity.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Quantifies the physical bottleneck behind the freight spike and the inventory drawdown risk at inland German terminals.
insights.quote: most barges were operating at around 25% of their cargo capacity as of 12 August

insights.claim: The cost of moving cargo from Rotterdam to Cologne reached EUR 80 per metric tonne in the week ending 7 August, up from EUR 17 per metric tonne in mid-June, while rates to Frankfurt climbed to EUR 150 from EUR 29 over the same period.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Roughly a five-fold move in weeks - the magnitude that closes inland product arbitrage and forces buyers onto rail and truck at a premium.
insights.quote: the cost of moving cargo from Rotterdam to Cologne reached €80 per metric tonne in the week ending 7 August, up from €17 per metric tonne in mid-June

insights.claim: Reduced barge capacity combined with elevated freight costs risks pressuring margins for inland refiners if conditions persist through August and September, historically the driest months for the Rhine basin.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: A seasonal-window trade: inland German refining margins are the direct P&L expression of Rhine levels, and the calendar works against them into September.
insights.locator: The combination of reduced barge capacity

insights.claim: Wood Mackenzie's VesselTracker recorded an improvement in Rhine conditions in the week before publication following rainfall across the basin, so the record-low episode was already partially unwinding.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: The European leg is mean-reverting on rainfall while the Panama leg is not - do not treat the two drought stories as a single persistent trade.
insights.locator: Wood Mackenzie's VesselTracker recorded an improvement

insights.claim: Monitoring El Niño-driven disruptions to canal operations and Gulf Coast logistics will be critical for staying ahead of further commodity flow dislocations through Q3 and Q4 2026.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Sets an explicit two-quarter watch horizon; weather and hydrology data become tradeable inputs for commodity flow forecasting.
insights.quote: Monitoring El Niño-driven disruptions to canal operations and Gulf Coast logistics will be critical for staying ahead of further commodity flow dislocations through Q3 and Q4 2026

insights.claim: Many regions, and particularly the Pacific, are already facing energy crunches, so shipping disruptions of this kind could further exacerbate markets that are already extremely tight.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Shocks landing on already-tight markets produce convex price responses - the asymmetry favours upside optionality over linear exposure.
insights.quote: As many regions, and particularly the Pacific, are facing energy crunches, disruptions like this could further exacerbate already extremely tight markets.
insights.locator: As many regions, and particularly the Pacific
